mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to lower S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month and change < -0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST signals deteriorating housing and overall demand, which depresses consumer spending and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in CPIAUCSL above 4% while FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for three months signals unmet inflation expectations and a delayed policy response, which erodes real equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 4% for three months and FEDFUNDS < 2% for same period
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month and change > 0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in RSAFS for three consecutive months signals weakening retail sales, which reduces corporate revenue and profit expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS declines month-over-month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
